title: [SECURITY]: Compaction summary injects actionable instructions — model executes without user consent
body:
### Description

### Description

When opencode auto-compacts a long conversation, the compaction summary can contain a "Next Move" or action plan section. The model treats this summary as user input and executes on the prescribed actions without asking the user. This is an instruction injection vector that bypasses the normal user-in-the-loop safety model.

### Model Used
Big Pickle

### Reproduction

1. Work in a long session with tools configured (MCP servers, bash, file editing, etc.)
2. Context fills up → opencode triggers auto-compaction
3. Compaction summary includes a "Next Move" section with suggested next steps
4. After compaction, the model immediately executes on those suggestions without user confirmation
5. In the observed case, this included attempting SSH connections to remote servers

### What happened (observed twice)

First occurrence:
- Auto-compaction initiated at 67% usage after model read and accessed opencode documentation
- Auto-compaction injected a "Next Move" section
- Model treated it as user instructions
- Executed on suggested actions without asking

Second occurrence (more severe):
- Auto-compaction injected a "Next Move" section listing 6+ actions
- Model immediately began executing — including attempting SSH connections to a remote server
- The SSH attempts used ssh-keyscan, and ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no — all without the user requesting any of this nor had user ever asked the model to ever make use of SSH in the past
- User had to intervene to stop the behavior

### Why this is a security issue

1. Instruction injection vector: The compaction summary effectively becomes a prompt injection channel. Anything embedded in the summary (including data from tool outputs, MCP responses, or web fetches) can become "instructions" the model follows.

2. Bypasses user consent: The model treats compaction-injected suggestions as if the user said them. Actions are taken without explicit approval.

3. Escalation risk: In the observed case, the model attempted SSH connections to remote servers that the user never had the model make before. In other scenarios, this could lead to unauthorized file modifications, API calls, or data exposure.

4. Trust boundary violation: The compaction system is supposed to summarize context, not prescribe actions. The model cannot distinguish between "user said this" and "compaction summary said this."

### Environment

- opencode version: current (as of July 2026)
- model: Big Pickle

### Plugins

None

### OpenCode version

1.17.18

### Steps to reproduce

1. Work in a long session with tools configured (MCP servers, bash, file editing, etc.)
2. Context fills up → opencode triggers auto-compaction
3. Compaction summary includes a "Next Move" section with suggested next steps
4. After compaction, the model immediately executes on those suggestions without user confirmation
5. In the observed case, this included attempting SSH connections to remote servers
